You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

# Outcome sub-dossier — DCT Industrial Trust Inc. business after combination with Prologis, ~3-5-year horizon

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. DCT Industrial Trust Inc. ceased to exist as a

> subsequent public filings were reviewed for any separately disclosed record of the
> acquired business. This sub-dossier contains no information about how the transaction
> was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- DCT Industrial Trust Inc. and DCT Industrial Operating Partnership LP filed a Form
  15-12B on 2018-11-09 (identified on the form as "Prologis, Inc., as successor by merger
  to DCT Industrial Trust Inc." and "Prologis, L.P., as successor by merger to DCT
  Industrial Operating Partnership LP"), certifying termination of registration of DCT
  common stock under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act, with the number of holders of
  record as of the notice date stated as "None." [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-18-323872,
  Form 15-12B]
- No Form 10-K or other periodic report was filed by DCT Industrial Trust Inc. (CIK
  1170991) after its final pre-merger annual report (filed 2018-02-16 for fiscal year
  2017); no subsequent annual or periodic filing appears under that CIK. [SRC:
  https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001170991&type=10-K]

## Search for a separately disclosed record of the acquired business
- Prologis, Inc.'s Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021 (filed 2022-02-09, within the 3-5-year
  window after the August 2018 closing) was reviewed in full; it contains no reference to
  "DCT," "DCT Industrial Trust," or "Industrial Trust" anywhere in the filing text. [SRC:
  SEC accession 0001564590-22-004436, Prologis Inc. Form 10-K for FY2021]
- That Form 10-K states Prologis's business comprises two operating segments, "Real Estate
  Operations and Strategic Capital," with no segment, sub-segment, or line item
  corresponding to the former DCT business. [SRC: SEC accession 0001564590-22-004436,
  Prologis Inc. Form 10-K for FY2021]
- No separate financial statements, segment disclosure, or narrative discussion isolating
  the performance of the properties or operations that had comprised DCT Industrial Trust
  Inc. was located in the reviewed filing. [SRC: SEC accession 0001564590-22-004436,
  Prologis Inc. Form 10-K for FY2021]

## Items not addressed
- Because no separate disclosure of the acquired business was located, no post-close
  outcome scalar (financial performance, disruption, divestiture, or otherwise) specific
  to the DCT business can be sourced for this dossier; any inference from Prologis's
  consolidated (whole-company) results would not isolate the acquired business and is
  therefore not reported here. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- DCT Industrial Trust Inc. terminated its SEC registration within roughly three months of
  the August 22, 2018 closing and filed no further periodic reports; a review of the
  acquiring company's Form 10-K three years after closing found no reference to DCT and no
  segment or disclosure isolating the former DCT business from the acquirer's consolidated
  operations. No public 3-5-year outcome record specific to the acquired business could be
  located; the outcome for this business is accordingly not publicly observable within the
  fixed window and is reported here as uncertain rather than inferred. [SRC: SEC accession
  0001193125-18-323872, Form 15-12B] [SRC: SEC accession 0001564590-22-004436, Prologis
  Inc. Form 10-K for FY2021]

[SLICE END]
